description: Corn smut is a fungal disease of maize that produces tumor-like galls on different parts of the plant. These galls contain masses of dark spores and can significantly reduce yield. In Mexico, immature galls are considered a culinary delicacy known as huitlacoche.

leaves: Small galls on leaf veins or blades
stems: Large galls on stalks or nodes
ears: Galls turn black and rupture releasing spores

disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil or crop debris as teliospores
Spores germinate and produce haploid sporidia
Compatible sporidia mate and form infectious hyphae
Tumor-like galls form and produce new teliospores
Spores spread by wind and rain
favorable_conditions: Wind and rain that spread spores
Periods of poor pollination or plant stress

chemical: Fungicides are generally ineffective for controlling corn smut

economic_importance: Usually causes low yield losses in field corn
Can significantly affect sweet corn production
Ear galls reduce market value of fresh corn
additional_notes: Immature galls are edible and sold as a gourmet food called huitlacoche in Mexico
The fungus is widely used as a model organism in fungal genetics and plant pathology research
